comments.comment:
I've just read the post, and coming from a woman who has never wanted children, or taken the pill, while being rather gung-ho sexually, yet never falling pregnant (had I become pregnant, I would have kept it - God's will, and all that), and no issue with abortion...whatever. I can't really relate.
Yet, if I must "yes, I'd be really angry too, if I was bullied out of keeping a baby!"

What a terrible response article from @askphilippa . I’m annoyed and genuinely shocked that someone who is supposed to care about people’s psychological wellbeing would express such a reactionary position. It is entirely possible to feel conflicted, sad, relieved, or emotionally complicated about an abortion and still know it was the right choice. Those feelings are not contradictions. To make assumptions about somebody’s family, relationships, or emotional life in such a simplistic way feels completely detached from the reality we actually live in. People can make choices about their own lives and bodies without those choices defining them as damaged. What a load of rubbish from someone who should know better.
